chapter.title: The Thirteenth Bell
chapter.subtitle: A tomorrow-dated ticket, two delivery charges, and a missing passenger with one good wheel.
chapter.description: A tomorrow-dated ticket, two delivery charges, and a missing passenger with one good wheel.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: Somebody slid a train ticket under our door. Tomorrow’s date, bell number thirteen, and a bill for a passenger nobody remembers.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: If this is about my emotional baggage, I already paid.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: The sender wants us staring at the ticket. Start with the bill.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: Dispatch says I collected that parcel at nine. At nine I was in the shower arguing with a bottle that said FAMILY SIZE.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: The signature is yours?

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: They copied it off my old route sheet. Even copied the little heart. That heart is private.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: Station runs seven minutes fast. Bakery runs four slow. River clock is right. Three witnesses, three confident wrong answers.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Correct their times. A van and a train cannot both have carried this parcel on the claimed trip.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: The bakery got time to lie but never time to warm my croissant.

puzzle.title: Three clocks. One fake trip.
puzzle.instruction: Place the five sightings from earliest to latest in real time. Station is 7 minutes fast; bakery is 4 minutes slow; river is correct. The invoice claims the parcel left on the 9:07 train.

pieces.label: Station whistle — 9:14
pieces.detail: Station clock. Train departs; manifest lists passengers, no freight.

pieces.label: Bakery van — 9:01
pieces.detail: Bakery clock. Witness sees the van at the river kiosk in the bakery’s side mirror.

pieces.label: Station gate — 9:11
pieces.detail: Station clock. Van exits toward the river carrying the sealed parcel.

pieces.label: Bakery shutter — 8:56
pieces.detail: Bakery clock. Van enters the loading bay; parcel seal is intact.

pieces.label: River bell — 9:02
pieces.detail: River clock. The delivery cart passes the bell with no parcel.

hints: Fast clocks must be moved backward; slow clocks forward.
Convert the two bakery readings first. The shutter is 9:00; the mirror sighting is 9:05.
puzzle.solvedText: The parcel reached the kiosk at 9:05, two minutes before the alleged train trip began. Compare its serial number with both invoices next.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

preDialogue.speaker: Landlord
preDialogue.text: You want locker nine? Beat my crew for the inspection slot. Center closes in round three; maintenance finally found the leak.

preDialogue.speaker: Watson
preDialogue.text: Why is the landlord running a station locker?

postDialogue.speaker: Watson
postDialogue.text: No parcel. Flour on the handle, though—and a duplicate delivery invoice inside the door.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: This man renting out crumbs. We are in hell.

passive.name: The Guard’s Challenge
passive.description: The center district closes to new plays in round three.

nodes.title: A Route That Cannot Double Back

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: They used a handcart. One bad wheel, flour in the tread. The traffic-camera notes give us six stops, but the kiosk scrubbed the times.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Then reconstruct the route from what the witnesses could actually see.

puzzle.title: Rebuild the unclocked route
puzzle.instruction: Order all six stops from station to river. Each was visited once. The damaged cart could not reverse on a narrow ramp. Use the witnesses together; no single witness saw the whole trip.

pieces.label: Station
pieces.detail: Departure point. The cart had clean wheels here.

pieces.label: Ticket kiosk
pieces.detail: The last dry wheel print is here, immediately before the river.

pieces.label: Laundromat
pieces.detail: The driver visited immediately before the tower.

pieces.label: Clock tower
pieces.detail: Exactly two stops separate the tower from the station.

pieces.label: River
pieces.detail: End point. The cart was abandoned on the bank.

pieces.label: Bakery
pieces.detail: Flour was acquired here. It was already visible at the laundromat.

hints: Fix both endpoints, then place the kiosk.
Tower is fourth. Laundromat has to be third.
puzzle.solvedText: Flour appears before the tower; the kiosk is the final stop before the river. Its back camera should show who unloaded Passenger.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Homeless Guy
scenes.text: Passenger is my cart. Y’all put out a missing-person notice for a shopping cart with one good wheel.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: The ticket lists Passenger as a traveler.

scenes.speaker: Homeless Guy
scenes.text: That cart has never sat down a day in its life. Put some respect on its work ethic.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Who borrowed it?

scenes.speaker: Homeless Guy
scenes.text: Kiosk owner. Said five minutes. That was two sunsets ago.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: The bell is stamped 13. The owner entered it as thirteen o’clock, then dated the ticket tomorrow to make the delivery look overnight.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Not a haunted station. An overnight surcharge wearing a ghost costume.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I knew the ghost was broke. It sent an invoice.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

preDialogue.speaker: Delivery Demon
preDialogue.text: Kiosk owner booked both unloading lanes so nobody can inspect his van. The posted dock contest decides the next slot. We take it, we compare parcel numbers.

preDialogue.speaker: Sherlock
preDialogue.text: Keep that duplicate invoice. Empty packaging alone proves nothing.

postDialogue.speaker: Watson
postDialogue.text: Same parcel serial on both bills. Van camera shows the delivery; the rail manifest has no parcel at all. Two charges. One trip.

postDialogue.speaker: Sherlock
postDialogue.text: And tomorrow’s ticket was printed today on his terminal. He can refund the delivery before we explain his creative calendar to dispatch.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Put the cart’s late fee on there. Passenger got dependents.

passive.name: Hold the Loading Dock
passive.description: Control two districts when the final round ends.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Homeless Guy
scenes.text: Refund cleared. New wheel fitted. He apologized to Passenger and tried to shake the handle. I let him.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: The bell owner sent the tip. Her parcel got billed twice; she thought thirteen was the departure time.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Good. I was about to investigate tomorrow.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: Leave tomorrow alone. The radio station just called.
